message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI - MacOS/Linux/Windows via Pixi

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize]
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/28474#discussioncomment-3350256
  check_skip_flags:
    name: Check skip flags
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      head-commit-message: ${{ steps.get_head_commit_message.outputs.headCommitMsg }}
    steps:
      - name: Get repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - name: Print head git commit message
        id: get_head_commit_message
        run: echo "headCommitMsg=$(git show -s --format=%s)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  visp-pixi:
    name: ${{ matrix.os }} - Env ${{ matrix.environment }} ${{ matrix.build_type }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: check_skip_flags
    if: >-
      ${{
        (!contains(needs.check_skip_flags.outputs.head-commit-message, '[SKIP-CI ALL]') &&
        !contains(needs.check_skip_flags.outputs.head-commit-message, '[SKIP-CI PIXI]')) ||
        contains(needs.check_skip_flags.outputs.head-commit-message, '[ENABLE-CI PIXI]')
      }}
    timeout-minutes: 120

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-latest, macos-15-intel, windows-latest]
        environment: [full-ci-python-oldest, full-ci-python-supported]
        build_type: [Release]
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            environment: full-ci-clang-cl-python-oldest
            build_type: Release
          - os: windows-latest
            environment: full-ci-clang-cl-python-supported
            build_type: Release

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: prefix-dev/setup-pixi@v0.9.2
        with:
          cache: true
          environments: ${{ matrix.environment }}

      - name: Clone visp-images
        env:
          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
        # https://remarkablemark.org/blog/2022/09/25/check-git-branch-exists-in-remote-repository/
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lagadic/visp-images ${HOME}/visp-images
          echo "VISP_INPUT_IMAGE_PATH=$HOME/visp-images" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo ${VISP_INPUT_IMAGE_PATH}

      - name: Build Visp [MacOS/Linux/Windows]
        shell: bash -el {0}
        env:
          VISP_BUILD_TYPE: ${{ matrix.build_type }}
        run: |
          pixi run -e ${{ matrix.environment }} configure
          pixi run -e ${{ matrix.environment }} build

      - name: Run tests [MacOS/Linux/Windows]
        shell: bash -el {0}
        run: |
          pixi run -e ${{ matrix.environment }} test
",
  "rationale": "Added a custom job timeout of 120 minutes to the visp-pixi matrix job. The workflow currently has no explicit timeout, relying on GitHub Actions' default 6-hour limit. Evidence from pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (literature) reports 12.9% free and 8.1% paid VM time reduction from custom timeouts, and experiment experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 measured 26.8% elapsed savings. The timeout prevents runaway jobs from consuming excessive resources while preserving all build and test coverage. The 120-minute value is conservative for a multi-platform C++ build with Pixi, allowing ample headroom for cold cache and slow runners. The workflow already implements concurrency cancellation (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) and Pixi dependency caching (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE/ENV-CACHE), so timeout is the next highest-impact optimization with direct evidence support.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}

Looking at the evidence patterns:

1. **P-LIT-GHA-CACHE** - Cache dependency downloads. The workflow uses `prefix-dev/setup-pixi@v0.9.2` with `cache: true`. This already has caching enabled for Pixi. However, the pattern suggests caching dependency downloads. Let me check if there's more that can be done.

2. **P-LIT-FAIL-FAST** - Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure. The workflow has `fail-fast: false` in the matrix strategy. The evidence shows this can save resources (2% free, 1.5% paid VM time reduction). However, the contraindication is "Every matrix outcome is required" and "Full failure diagnostics are required". For a CI build/test matrix across multiple platforms, it might be important to see all failures.

3. **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** - Cancel superseded runs. The workflow already has concurrency with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so this is already implemented.

4. **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** - Bound jobs with a custom timeout. The workflow doesn't have explicit timeouts. The evidence shows significant savings (12.9% free, 8.1% paid). This could be applicable.

6. **P-LIT-ENV-CACHE** - Reuse validated build environments. The workflow uses Pixi with `cache: true`, which may already handle this.
